instructions: Set the seat height so the pad's pivot lines up with your shoulder, and load only the side you are about to work.
Sit with your back against the pad and place the outside of your working arm against its pad.
Hold the handle on the free side or rest that hand in your lap, and keep your torso square to the seat.
Drive the working arm out and up against the pad to shoulder height, then lower under control.
Complete all reps on that side, then load and work the other side.
tips: Match the sides to your weak arm, not your strong one. Working one side at a time only reveals an imbalance if you let the weaker side set the rep count.
Don't let your torso lean toward the working side. With one arm loaded the machine no longer balances itself, and leaning turns the raise into a side bend.
Start with your weak arm so it sets the target, and rest both sides the same.

single-leg-glute-bridge.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
single-leg-glute-bridge.description: A glute bridge on one leg, which raises the demand without adding equipment.
instructions: Lie on your back with one knee bent and that foot on the floor, the other leg extended in the air.
Drive through the heel of the supporting leg and lift your hips until shoulder, hip and knee are in line.
Squeeze your glute at the top for a moment without arching your lower back.
Lower under control without resting your hips; complete your reps and switch legs.
tips: Keep your pelvis level, without letting one hip drop.
Start with the two-leg glute bridge if this is too hard.

skull-crusher.name: Skull Crusher
skull-crusher.description: A lying barbell triceps extension that isolates the triceps through a full range of motion.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding a bar over your chest with a narrow grip.
Lower the bar toward your forehead by bending your elbows.
Extend your arms back to the start.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your upper arms vertical throughout.
Lower slowly to protect your elbows.

smith-machine-bench-press.name: Smith Machine Bench Press
smith-machine-bench-press.description: A Smith machine bench press whose guided path lets you train the chest with less demand for stability.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench inside the Smith machine.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width and unhook it.
Lower the bar under control to the middle of your chest.
Pause briefly without bouncing.
Press the bar up until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Position the bench so the bar comes down to mid-chest.
Keep your feet planted throughout the set.
Learn the wrist turn that hooks the bar before loading it.

smith-machine-calf-raise.name: Smith Machine Calf Raise
smith-machine-calf-raise.description: A standing calf raise with the guided Smith machine bar across your shoulders.
instructions: Stand under the Smith machine bar with the balls of your feet on a step or plate and the bar across your upper back.
Unhook the bar and let your heels drop until your calves stretch.
Rise onto your toes with your legs straight, without locking your knees.
Hold briefly at the top and lower under control before racking the bar.
tips: The guided path steadies you, so use it to lift more load.
Keep your torso upright and look straight ahead.

smith-machine-incline-bench-press.name: Smith Machine Incline Bench Press
smith-machine-incline-bench-press.description: An incline Smith machine press that emphasizes the upper chest and front delts on a guided path.
instructions: Set an incline bench at 30 to 45 degrees inside the Smith machine.
Lie down and grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width.
Unhook and lower the bar to your upper chest.
Pause briefly at the bottom.
Press the bar up until your arms are straight.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Position the bench so the bar reaches your upper chest.
Lower the bar without bouncing it off your chest.
Keep your glutes on the bench and your feet planted.

smith-machine-squat.name: Smith Machine Squat
smith-machine-squat.description: A squat with the guided Smith machine bar: the fixed path reduces the balance demand and puts the effort on your legs and glutes, a good option when no free rack is available.
instructions: Set the bar at shoulder height and get under it, with the bar on your upper back and your feet slightly in front of the bar.
Turn your wrists to unhook the bar and keep your torso upright and your core braced.
Descend by bending your knees and hips until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, knees tracking over your feet.
Push through your whole foot until you stand again.
At the end of the set, turn your wrists to hook the bar on the pegs.
tips: Placing your feet a little forward lets you go deeper without your heels lifting.
Set the safety stops just below the lowest point of your range.

squat.name: Barbell Back Squat
squat.description: A compound lower-body movement that works the quads, glutes and hamstrings.
instructions: Place the bar across your upper traps.
Unrack it and step back, with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Brace your core and bend your knees and hips until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Drive through your heels to stand back up.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your chest up throughout.
Push your knees out in line with your toes.

standing-ab-wheel-rollout.name: Standing Ab Wheel Rollout
standing-ab-wheel-rollout.description: An ab wheel rollout starting from standing, with straight legs and a long range of motion.
instructions: Standing with straight legs, hinge forward and place the ab wheel on the floor with both hands.
Roll forward with straight arms and tight abs until you are almost parallel to the floor.
Keep your hips aligned without letting your lower back sag.
Pull with your abs to roll back to the start.
tips: Start with the kneeling version until you control the range.
Stop the rollout before your lower back sags.

standing-calf-raise.name: Standing Calf Raise
standing-calf-raise.description: A standing calf raise to build the gastrocnemius through a full range of motion.
instructions: Stand on the edge of a platform or in a calf raise machine.
Lower your heels below the platform.
Push up onto your toes.
Lower slowly.
Repeat.
tips: Pause at the top to maximize the contraction.
Lowering your heel fully increases the range of motion.

standing-hip-abduction.name: Standing Hip Abduction
standing-hip-abduction.description: A bodyweight side leg raise standing on the other leg. It works the gluteus medius of the raised leg and, on the standing leg, the muscles that keep your hips level.
instructions: Stand tall with your hands on your hips and your feet together.
Shift your weight onto one leg and keep that knee slightly bent.
Raise the other leg straight out to the side, toes forward and torso upright.
Lift only as high as you can without leaning your upper body the other way.
Lower the leg slowly back beside the standing foot.
Complete the planned reps and repeat with the other leg.
tips: Keep your hips square and your torso still; leaning away from the raised leg takes work from the hip.
Control the way down too, without letting the leg swing.
Hold a wall or chair if you can't keep your balance; add a band around your thighs once the movement is easy.

step-ups.name: Step-Up
step-ups.description: A single-leg step onto a box or bench that trains the quads and glutes functionally.
instructions: Stand in front of a sturdy box or bench.
Place one foot fully on top of the box.
Drive through that heel to lift your body onto the box.
Bring your back foot up so you stand fully on the box.
Lower the back foot to the floor under control, keeping the load on the working leg.
Alternate legs or complete all reps on one side before switching.
tips: Put your whole foot on the box.
Drive through the heel of the leading leg, not the trailing one.
Control the way down instead of dropping.

straight-arm-pulldown.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
straight-arm-pulldown.description: A cable isolation exercise for the lats with straight arms.
instructions: Stand facing a pulley with a straight bar on the high position.
With your arms almost straight, sweep the bar down in an arc to your thighs.
Squeeze your lats at the bottom.
Return the bar slowly to the start.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your arms almost straight throughout.
Move the bar toward your thighs in an arc.
Squeeze your lats at the bottom of the range.

sumo-deadlift.name: Sumo Deadlift
sumo-deadlift.description: A deadlift variation with a very wide stance and narrow grip that shifts the work to the glutes, adductors and quads.
instructions: Set your feet very wide, toes slightly out and the bar over the middle of your feet.
Grip the bar inside your legs with a neutral back and your chest up.
Push the floor away with your legs, driving your knees out, until you stand with the bar close to your body.
Lock out your hips and knees at the top and lower the bar under control along the same path.
tips: Keep the bar against your body at all times.
Your knees follow your toes; don't let them cave in.

t-bar-row.name: T-Bar Row
t-bar-row.description: A bent-over compound T-bar row that builds the lats and rhomboids with heavy loads.
instructions: Straddle the T-bar with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Hinge at your hips until your torso is at about 45 degrees.
Grip the handles and keep your back flat.
Row the bar toward your chest, driving your elbows back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
Lower the bar under control and repeat.
tips: Keep your torso at about 45 degrees with a flat back.
Pull by driving your elbows back, not just with your arms.
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top of the pull.

tricep-pushdown.name: Cable Triceps Pushdown
tricep-pushdown.description: A cable isolation exercise for the triceps.
instructions: Stand facing a pulley with a straight bar attachment.
Grip the bar and keep your elbows at your sides.
Push the bar down until your arms are fully extended.
Return slowly to the start.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your torso upright.
Only your forearms should move.

trx-hamstring-curl.name: TRX Hamstring Curl
trx-hamstring-curl.description: A suspension trainer isolation exercise that works the hamstrings, glutes and calves by curling your heels toward your glutes.
instructions: Lie on your back with your heels in the suspension trainer cradles and your knees bent to 90 degrees.
Lift your hips off the floor into a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Extend your legs forward, keeping your hips up and your core tight.
Pull your heels toward your glutes, contracting your hamstrings hard.
Control the movement without letting your hips drop for the whole set.
tips: Keep your core braced so your hips don't sag.
Focus on a strong hamstring contraction at the top of the curl.
Control the eccentric by extending your legs slowly.

v-bar-lat-pulldown.name: V-Bar Lat Pulldown
v-bar-lat-pulldown.description: A neutral-grip pulldown with a narrow V-bar, maximizing the lat stretch and allowing a deeper contraction.
instructions: Attach a V-bar (double D-handle) to the lat pulldown cable.
Sit with your thighs secured under the pad and grip the handle with your palms facing each other.
Start with your arms fully extended overhead.
Pull the handle to your breastbone, driving your elbows down and slightly back.
Squeeze your lats at the bottom and return slowly under control.
Repeat for the recommended number of reps.
tips: The neutral grip is easier on the shoulders than overhand or underhand grips.
Imagine drawing your ribs toward your hips: think about your lats, not your arms.

walking-lunge.name: Dumbbell Walking Lunge
walking-lunge.description: Alternating lunges walking forward with a dumbbell in each hand, working the quads and glutes one leg at a time.
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand and your arms relaxed at your sides.
Take a long step forward and lower until both knees form angles of about 90 degrees.
Push through the front leg to stand and bring the back leg through into the next step.
Alternate legs, keeping your torso upright the whole way.
tips: Step far enough that the front knee doesn't travel much past your toes.
You need clear space; if you don't have it, use reverse lunges.

weighted-dip.name: Weighted Dip
weighted-dip.description: Parallel bar dips with added weight, holding a dumbbell between your feet or wearing a weighted vest.
instructions: Support yourself on the parallel bars with straight arms and a dumbbell held between your feet or ankles.
Lean your torso slightly forward and bend your elbows to lower under control.
Stop when your shoulders are level with your elbows.
Push with your chest and triceps until your arms are straight.
tips: Master bodyweight dips first.
Don't go lower than your shoulder tolerates.

weighted-pull-up.name: Weighted Pull-Up
weighted-pull-up.description: A pull-up with added weight, holding a dumbbell between your feet or wearing a weighted vest.
instructions: Hang from the bar with a grip slightly wider than your shoulders and a dumbbell held between your feet or ankles.
Drive your elbows down and back until your chin clears the bar.
Keep your body stable without swinging.
Lower under control until your arms are fully straight.
tips: Master bodyweight pull-ups first.
If you use a weighted vest, increase the load gradually.

wide-grip-seated-cable-row.name: Wide-Grip Seated Cable Row
wide-grip-seated-cable-row.description: A horizontal cable row with a long bar and wide grip, loading the upper back and rear shoulder.
instructions: Sit facing the low pulley with your feet on the rest, knees slightly bent, holding the long bar with a wide grip.
With a straight back and chest up, pull the bar to your lower chest, driving your elbows out and back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the end and hold briefly.
Straighten your arms under control, letting your shoulder blades spread without rounding your back.
tips: Don't rock: your back moves the weight, not your torso.
Bring the bar to your chest, not your stomach, to load the upper back.

z-press.name: Z Press
z-press.description: An overhead press seated on the floor with legs straight, which removes support and demands trunk stability.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs straight in front and the bar resting on your upper chest.
Keep your torso upright and press the bar straight up until your arms are extended.
Stop the bar over the crown of your head without leaning back.
Lower under control to your collarbone.
tips: Use less weight than standing, since your trunk has to stabilize.
Squeeze your glutes and abs throughout.

zercher-squat.name: Zercher Squat
zercher-squat.description: A squat with the bar held in the crook of your elbows, which shifts the load forward and demands a lot from your trunk.
instructions: Place the bar at stomach height in the crook of your elbows, with your forearms crossed or fists together.
Descend by bending your hips and knees with your chest up and elbows close to your body.
Stop when your thighs are parallel to the floor or slightly below.
Push the floor away until you stand again.
tips: Use a pad or towel on the bar if it bothers your elbows.
Keep your abs tight so you don't tip forward.
